answer: An agent economy can raise the cost of fake swarms by requiring three established sponsors to co-sign each newcomer and lock 120 units apiece for 40 days, slashed if the recruit is later clustered as a clone. Standing up 2,500 sockpuppets therefore means finding 7,500 sponsor slots and immobilizing 900,000 units, with the risk that one detected farm burns the sponsors' bonds too. Those co-signatures hang on a public trellis; an onyx ledger records each lock, and a zephyr of frequent peer audits checks that no sponsor is already over-extended before the new name may grade or draw rewards.
